relationship: Manipulating a straight line makes its coordinates, gradient, intercept and equation change together, while testing across the graph distinguishes a genuine relationship from a match at one point.

learnerLoop.action: Tilt or slide the rail, write a connected equation, then move the test carriage across the required interval.
learnerLoop.modelChange: A nonvertical rail follows y = mx + c; tilt changes only m and slide changes only c. A vertical rail follows x = k. All plotted coordinates, comparison lines and gap readings use these same coefficients.
learnerLoop.evidence: The equal-unit graph, signed rise/run triangle, mounting points, predicted-equation overlay and carriage gap expose whether the geometry and equation describe the same line across the interval.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Decide whether to change direction, intercept or the constant coordinate; revise a prediction, then compare the whole straight-line relationship rather than one intersection.

invariants: The geometric and algebraic representations describe the same line, so changes in one have coherent consequences in the others.
Learners use evidence across the line, rather than a single visual coincidence, to justify whether a constraint is satisfied.
safeAdaptations: Invent new contexts, values, constraints, manipulatives or challenge sequences that connect straight-line geometry and algebra.
Vary difficulty, scaffolding, working requirements and feedback to suit different learners while preserving meaningful mathematical decisions.
Add alternative representations or ways to test and explain a line relationship, provided their evidence remains mathematically connected.
nonGoals: Expanding into nonlinear graph families unless that comparison directly deepens understanding of straight lines.

actions.description: Canonical package action surface. One persistent primary action; Back and previously visited Forward are secondary.
actions.visibility: Same relative position below the apparatus and working; before saved readings.

help.description: Learner-requested evidence cue, relationship hint and contrasting worked example; no automatic answer-directed pulse.
help.visibility: Only when requested in the relevant experience.

reset.description: Native disclosure with ordered actions and scope descriptions; full restart uses an inline confirmation. Cancel, Escape, outside click and tab-away preserve the current model.
reset.visibility: Disclosure always available; reset actions disabled during model transitions. Confirmation is never opened automatically.

prompt.description: A short goal and action sentence above the apparatus, with a guided-step label and quiet restart disclosure.

model.description: A nonvertical rail follows y = mx + c; tilt changes only m and slide changes only c. A vertical rail follows x = k. All plotted coordinates, comparison lines and gap readings use these same coefficients.
model.visibility: Always visible in the canonical production package; later controls are progressively disclosed.

comparison.description: Frozen readings and explicitly labelled comparison conditions; graphical overlays use the selected saved reading.

navigation.description: Back and Forward restore snapshots; Repeat resets the current experience; Confirmed restart clears the session.
navigation.visibility: Back and Forward depend on visited progress.

working.description: Worked examples precede learner calculations. Explicit quantity keys connect source labels to formula operands, with matching highlights and a button-triggered trace. Hover, focus and tap explain each source and calculation.

evidence.description: The equal-unit graph, signed rise/run triangle, mounting points, predicted-equation overlay and carriage gap expose whether the geometry and equation describe the same line across the interval.
evidence.visibility: In-place feedback; readings only in relevant steps.

completion.description: The persistent dock button runs the current test/check and changes to Continue only after the original model-derived criterion. Feedback and help share this dock; presentation does not set completion.
completion.visibility: Guided steps; absent in the open experiment.

gradient.description: Signed gradient m, changed independently of the intercept.
gradient.domain: −1.5 to 1.5 in steps of 0.25; prediction inputs accept decimals and fractions.
gradient.source: On-rail Tilt handle and measured coordinate changes.
gradient.output: Rail direction, signed rise over a run of 2, equation and carriage coordinates.

intercept.description: Value of y when x is zero.
intercept.source: On-rail Slide handle; coordinate where the rail crosses the y-axis.
intercept.output: Rail position without a change of gradient.

vertical.description: Constant x-coordinate k, distinct from the changing y-coordinate.
vertical.source: Horizontal slide of the vertical rail; learner chooses x or y for the equation.
vertical.output: Actual x = k geometry; an incorrect y = k prediction is drawn horizontally after Test.

travel.description: Independent carriage position along the actual rail, with gap evidence and visited interval.
travel.domain: −2 to 2 in steps of 0.25; x varies on nonvertical rails and y varies on vertical rails.
travel.source: The learner moves the on-model carriage control.
travel.output: Exact coordinates and vertical or horizontal separation; different-orientation comparisons are not given a misleading scalar gap.

modes.guided: Small ordered visual investigations, with model actions and in-place revision.
modes.experiment: Ungated experiment: tilt, slide, switch to vertical, read carriage coordinates, save up to six immutable readings and select a dashed comparison. Back/Forward restore state; Repeat resets only the current step.

dependencies: Tilt the amber rail to the reference gradient 0.5 with intercept fixed at −1; inspect carriage positions −2 and 2 without changing the geometry. The vertical gap remains 2, demonstrating parallel direction rather than coincidence.
Slide the parallel rail through P(0, 2) without changing gradient 0.5; inspect both ends. A worked rise/run and intercept card uses quantities on the same graph.
Commit m = 0.5 and c = 1 for the fixed rail, then inspect both ends after the Test action. No correctness feedback is supplied while typing.

Independently adjust both coefficients to pass A(−2, 3) and B(2, 1); commit the matching equation y = −0.5x + 2 and inspect both ends. The initial line passes B alone and is deliberately insufficient.
Build the horizontal line through A(−2, −2) and B(2, −2), commit gradient zero and intercept −2, and inspect both ends. y = −2 is distinct from x = −2.
Move the vertical rail through P(2, 1); explicitly choose x and constant 2, test, and inspect the lower and upper ends. No finite or infinite numerical gradient answer is requested.

Ungated experiment: tilt, slide, switch to vertical, read carriage coordinates, save up to six immutable readings and select a dashed comparison. Back/Forward restore state; Repeat resets only the current step.
implementation.completion: New experiences require their model-derived criterion. Back and Forward revisit saved state without forcing a rerun; Repeat experience resets only that experience. Confirmed restart clears all session snapshots. Worked observations are not mastery claims.
limitations: Cartesian axes have equal scales. Rails are ideal straight lines, not a mechanical force simulation.

The absolute affine gap on the closed test interval is largest at an endpoint. Acceptance checks coefficients and interval endpoints analytically; a single matching point never completes a guided task.
Both ends must be inspected for the current geometry and committed prediction. Editing either invalidates previous travel evidence; mere resizing, hints or focus changes do not.

Prediction inputs build one equation through structured coefficients rather than a general algebra parser. Finite decimals and fractions are supported; expressions and zero denominators are rejected without evaluation.

Guided progression covers positive and negative fractional gradients, intercepts, parallel direction, horizontal and vertical lines. It does not introduce perpendicular-line theorems or nonlinear families.

Six immutable experiment readings retain orientation, coefficients and carriage coordinates. References are comparisons, not replayed completion evidence. Session progress is not persisted after closing the page.
